boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Arkansas, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop for getting oriented, finding campus gathering spaces, and trying a few Razorback traditions.

cards.title: Friday: Check the A-Week schedule
cards.subtitle: New-student programming across campus
cards.notes: Open the current schedule and choose one activity that fits your arrival time; A-Week is designed to help first-year students transition to campus.
cards.short_summary: Use the university’s welcome-week program as a simple starting point for meeting people and learning campus routines.
cards.evidence_claim: A-Week runs after student move-in until fall classes begin and focuses on academic success, belonging, wellness, history and tradition, and involvement.
cards.access_notes: Programming, dates, locations, and participation details vary; consult the current A-Week schedule.

cards.title: Friday: Get your bearings at Old Main
cards.subtitle: Historic campus centerpiece
cards.notes: Walk to Old Main, take in the twin towers, and use the lawn as a visual reference point before heading to your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: Start with the building that anchors the Hill and its oldest campus landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Main has welcomed students since 1875 and is the university’s oldest structure.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing is appropriate; follow posted access guidance for interior spaces.

cards.title: Friday: Trace names along Senior Walk
cards.subtitle: Beginning near Old Main
cards.notes: Follow the engraved walk from Old Main and look for names at a comfortable pace; it is an easy way to connect campus paths with its history.
cards.short_summary: A walking stop built around the university’s long-running graduate-name tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Senior Walk begins near Old Main, winds across campus, and includes names of University of Arkansas graduates beginning with the class of 1876.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor pedestrian route; use accessible campus paths as needed.

cards.title: Friday: Pause in the Arkansas Union
cards.subtitle: 435 N. Garland Ave.
cards.notes: Use the common areas to regroup, ask at the information desk, or scan the building’s event listings before choosing the next part of your evening.
cards.short_summary: The central campus building combines gathering space, services, student involvement, dining, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arkansas Union provides dining, entertainment, meeting and event spaces, and student-involvement connections; it also has common spaces for meeting, relaxing, and studying.
cards.source_title: Student Activities | Arkansas Union | University of Arkansas
cards.access_notes: Building access and available spaces can vary with university operations and scheduled events.

cards.title: Saturday: Walk the Union Mall
cards.subtitle: Between the Arkansas Union and Mullins Library
cards.notes: Take the direct outdoor route between the Union and Mullins Library, then check whether an information table or campus event is using the mall.
cards.short_summary: A straightforward outdoor connector that doubles as an event and tabling area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Union Mall is the large area extending from the Arkansas Union to Mullins Library, with reservable information-table and event areas.
cards.source_title: Event Venues | Arkansas Union | University of Arkansas
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is generally open, but parts of the mall may be reserved for events.

cards.title: Saturday: Find the Greek Theatre
cards.subtitle: Outdoor campus amphitheater
cards.notes: Stop by the stone amphitheater in daylight and note its layout for future concerts, pep rallies, movies, or a quiet break between activities.
cards.short_summary: An identifiable outdoor venue with both campus-history and event-use context.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chi Omega Greek Theatre, donated in 1930, is used for concerts, pep rallies, and enjoying time outdoors between classes.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access and event setup can vary; respect any posted restrictions.

cards.title: Saturday: Learn the UREC Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Arkansas Union, second floor
cards.notes: If you have a valid university or UREC ID, locate the second-floor fitness center and decide whether its equipment or group-exercise room fits your routine.
cards.short_summary: A centrally located campus recreation facility for students and eligible UREC users.
cards.evidence_claim: The UREC Fitness Center is on the second floor of the Arkansas Union and includes nearly 6,000 square feet of gym floor space plus a group-exercise room.
cards.source_title: UREC Fitness Center | University of Arkansas
cards.access_notes: A valid University of Arkansas or UREC ID is required for entry; consult the official page for current hours.

cards.title: Saturday: Try the bouldering wall
cards.subtitle: HPER 102
cards.notes: If you are eligible to enter, check in at UREC Outdoors and try a short bouldering session; use the provided shoes and follow staff safety direction.
cards.short_summary: An indoor climbing option with equipment supplied for eligible participants.
cards.evidence_claim: The UREC Outdoors Bouldering Wall is in HPER 102, is free for valid UA student ID holders, UREC members, or valid guest-pass holders, and provides shoes at no additional charge.
cards.source_title: Bouldering Wall | UREC | University of Arkansas
cards.access_notes: Check in using the UREC app barcode or UARK ID; official page lists weekday hours and safety policies.

cards.title: Saturday: Look for a Union Theater program
cards.subtitle: Inside the Arkansas Union
cards.notes: Check the Union’s current event calendar for a movie, performance, ceremony, or other program, and verify entry details before making it your evening plan.
cards.short_summary: A named campus theater that hosts a range of university programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Union Theater is a 247-capacity, stadium-seating venue used for plays, ceremonies, performers, and movie showings.
cards.source_title: Event Venues | Arkansas Union | University of Arkansas
cards.access_notes: Programs and admission requirements vary by event; verify the current listing before attending.

cards.title: Sunday: Learn the Razorback call
cards.subtitle: University tradition
cards.notes: Before a future campus spirit event, learn the call’s place in Arkansas tradition and join only when the setting and organizers invite participation.
cards.short_summary: A school-specific shared ritual that connects students, alumni, and athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Arkansas materials identify Calling the Hogs as a distinctive campus tradition and a symbol represented on the official university ring.
cards.source_title: Spring Ring Ceremony and Graduate Farewell Celebrate Graduating Seniors | Arkansas News
cards.access_notes: This is a participatory tradition; follow event staff and venue guidance when it is used at an organized program.
